'Missing' Baptiste serving prison sentence in Morocco
- Published
An English athletics coach and former gold medallist said by media reports to be missing is serving a prison sentence in Morocco, BBC Sport can reveal.
Leon Baptiste, who was coaching a clutch of top British track athletes in the run-up to this summer's Commonwealth Games and European Championships, suddenly went off the grid more than three months ago.
Neither UK Athletics, for whom he worked as a consultant sprinting coach, nor the sprinters he coached knew why he was out of contact.
In May, Baptiste sent the group of athletes he coached a short message saying he would be absent from training "for a while". They have been given no further explanation.
Over the weekend, he was reported in the media as being "missing" and was said to have disappeared in Morocco.
On Tuesday, a brief email was sent to the people coached by Baptiste - the 200m gold medallist at the 2010 Commonwealth Games - in which he resigned from the position, citing unspecified ill health.
A source at the Moroccan Ministry of Justice confirmed to BBC Sport that Baptiste was arrested in Marrakech in May, has subsequently been convicted and is now serving a custodial sentence in Al-Oudaya prison.
"In relation to the reports concerning the alleged 'disappearance of Leon Baptiste' - an English athletics coach reportedly missing in Morocco for more than two months under questionable circumstances - please note that the information published in this regard is inaccurate and does not reflect the facts of the case," said the source.
"The foreign national concerned had not lost contact with his surroundings and was not subject to any disappearance or unexplained absence.
"He is currently being held at the local prison in Marrakech, where he is serving a custodial sentence following his conviction by the competent judicial authorities in connection with a misdemeanour case."
They added Baptiste, 41, was "in good health".
No details of what he was convicted of, or the length of his sentence, were provided.
The MMJ source said that was not uncommon in the Moroccan judicial system.
A spokesperson for the Morocco Public Prosecution Office confirmed: "The British national is currently being held at the local prison in Marrakech, where he is serving a custodial sentence following a court judgment against him in connection with his involvement in a criminal case."
Asked directly about Baptiste, a UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "We are supporting a British national who is detained in Morocco and are in contact with the authorities."
Sources told BBC Sport that Baptiste travelled to Marrakech with three other British former athletes, who have all since returned to the UK.
BBC Sport has made attempts to contact the athletes but had no reply.
Baptiste's family are understood to be aware of his imprisonment.
Baptiste's absence left some British sprinters - including Olympic bronze medallist Charlie Dobson, Paralympic gold medallist Sophie Hahn and Paralympic silver medallist Zac Shaw - without a designated coach before the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and European Championships in Birmingham.
Four-time European gold medallist Adam Gemili and relay coach Martyn Rooney stepped in to provide extra assistance to the athletes affected by Baptiste's abrupt departure.
But BBC Sport has been told the sprinters' training was heavily disrupted during a crucial period of their careers, leaving them ill-prepared and frustrated.
Those close to Baptiste who BBC Sport has spoken to describe him as a highly professional and dedicated coach with a reserved personality who keeps his private life to himself.
BBC Sport has approached UK Athletics for comment.
How did 'missing' reports turn into news of a prison sentence?
Once Baptiste's disappearance was reported in the media last weekend, BBC Sport began investigating his whereabouts.
We contacted a variety of figures in the British athletics community, people who know Baptiste, the UK Foreign Office, and authorities in Morocco in order to piece together the timeline of events.
It quickly became clear that Baptiste's whereabouts were known but his status was being withheld.
But Moroccan authorities confirmed details of Baptiste's case to BBC Sport when asked to do so.

Colombia’s far-right president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has announced a crackdown on immigrants, ordering authorities to detain and deport people who are in the country irregularly or have committed crimes.
In office for just over two weeks, the millionaire former lawyer made the announcement on Sunday as the country continued to grapple with the aftermath of a 7.4-magnitude earthquake on 10 August that killed more than 300 people and destroyed more than 30,000 homes.
De la Espriella said the first joint operations involving the police and the migration authority should begin “this very week”.
“Let the coordinated operations begin to track down illegal immigrants: first, those committing crimes; second, those who have not regularised their status and who will have to be deported immediately,” de la Espriella said during a cabinet meeting held on Sunday in Barranquilla, the Caribbean city that has in effect been turned into an alternative capital.
He echoed the “Americans first” rhetoric of his ally, US president Donald Trump, saying that from now on it would be “Colombians first, Colombians second and Colombians third”.
The Colombian president has joined other Trump-aligned leaders in the region who have also tightened migration rules, including Argentina’s Javier Milei and Chile’s José Antonio Kast.
De la Espriella’s order is facing criticism from the opposition and human rights activists, who say it will end a migration policy that endured for more than a decade under both rightwing and leftwing governments and benefited above all migrants fleeing the humanitarian crisis in neighbouring Venezuela.
Although he used the anti-immigration rhetoric characteristic of other far-right candidates during his campaign, his platform focused chiefly on his promise to pursue an iron-fist policy against criminal groups.
In the same announcement, he also declared that all gangs involved in drug trafficking, illegal mining, extortion and smuggling were “terrorists and we will treat them as such. Whatever happens, we will defeat them, by reason or by force.”
The president did not directly mention Venezuelans when discussing immigration, but they account for roughly 90% of all migrants in the country. Of the 2.8 million Venezuelans living in Colombia, about 848,000 are in an irregular situation, including 193,000 children and adolescents.
The leftwing senator María José Pizarro Rodríguez reposted the president’s announcement and asked whether he was “proposing a Colombian ICE against fellow Latin Americans”, in reference to the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). She added that the “order to deport irregular migrants is pure xenophobia and aporophobia”.
“Instead of persecuting people fleeing poverty and violence, regularise their status. There are thousands of migrants who work hard and contribute to the economies of the countries that receive them,” she wrote.
The Colombian newspaper El Tiempo reported that sources within the migration department believe the agency does not have enough staff to carry out the operations De la Espriella has promised.
Analysts have also noted that under Colombian law there is no such category as an “illegal” immigrant, as De la Espriella said, but rather migrants in an “irregular” situation, since being in the country without the proper documentation is not a crime.

D2C brand Epigamia’s existing shareholders Verlinvest and the family of its late cofounder Rohan Mirchandani have increased their stakes in the startup through a secondary transaction valued at $20 Mn. Sauce.vc also joined Epigamia’s cap table as part of the transaction. The deal involved the purchase of shares from existing investors and did not result in any fresh capital infusion into the startup. DSG Consumer Partners and Deepika Padukone’s investment firm KA Enterprises were among the selling shareholders in the transaction. The selling investors sold a portion of their stakes. Verlinvest first backed the startup in 2016 as part of its $6 Mn Series A funding round. It subsequently increased its stake through participation in multiple funding rounds. “The strengthened commitment from Verlinvest, the Mirchandani family, and the new institutional commitment from Sauce is a strong endorsement of the business we have built and the opportunity ahead,” Epigamia CEO Ritesh Gauba said. He added that the transaction would give Epigamia a stable shareholder base to support its next phase of growth. To date, Epigamia has raised around $60 Mn from investors including Verlinvest, Danone Manifesto Ventures, DSG Consumer Partners, Padukone, among others. Add DL funding chart The secondary transaction comes a few months after Epigamia appointed Gauba as its CEO in May. He has more than 24 years of experience in the FMCG sector and has previously worked with companies including Mars and Britannia. Around the same time, Epigamia elevated COO Ankur Goel to the role of cofounder. Following Mirchandani’s death in December 2024, Goel had been overseeing the startup’s operations alongside cofounder Uday Thakker and growth head Ajinkya Poundrik. Founded in 2015 by Mirchandani, Thakker, Krishnamoorthy, and Rahul Jain, Epigamia began as a Greek yoghurt brand before expanding its portfolio to include artisanal curd, snack packs, mishti doi, and smoothies. The startup sells its products through its website, ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, and offline retail stores. It claims to have a distribution network spanning more than 25,000 retail touchpoints across over 30 cities. Epigamia is yet to file its financial statements for FY25. Its net loss declined almost 74% to ₹17.4 Cr in FY24 from ₹67 Cr in the previous fiscal year. Operating revenue rose 3.3% to ₹173.7 Cr from ₹168.1 Cr during the period.

At 22,000 feet, -15°C: DRDO pulls off high-altitude combat parachute test
The trial was conducted at Dropzone, in one of the world’s highest altitude zones in the Leh district of Ladakh.
The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on Wednesday successfully tested a Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS) at Dropzone, in one of the world’s highest altitude zones in the Leh district of Ladakh.
The test for the system – designed by DRDO’s Aerial Delivery Research and Development Establishment – was carried out by Wing Commander Rahul Jha, chief test jumper and MWO R J Singh, VM(G), MWO Vivek Tiwari. The trio executed the jump from a height of 22,000 feet above mean sea level (AMSL), where the temperature was −15°C.
“Military Combat Parachute System (MCPS) designed and developed by ADRDE, DRDO was successfully tested at one of the world’s highest altitudes Drop Zones (Nyoma, Mudh DZ),” the DRDO said in a post on X.
“ADRDE test Jumpers Wg Cdr Rahul Jha Chief Test Jumper, MWO R J Singh, VM(G), MWO Vivek Tiwari executed the jump from 22,000 feet AMSL wherein the temperature was −15°C and utilised MCPS and all other sub-systems including indigenous para computer, oxygen system & jumpsuits. The parachute was deployed at 20,000 ft, with a safe landing at 13,700 ft,” it added.
The DRDO also said “the successful trial demonstrated the efficacy, reliability and tactical employability of MCPS in extreme high-altitude conditions, reinforcing India’s commitment to self-reliance in critical defence technologies.”

Cellulitis is a common bacterial infection that can be treated with a course of antibiotics. This skin infection is caused by a bacteria entering the system through broken skin, a wound or contracted by those with weak immune systems. The infection can affect the subcutaneous tissues, and is commonly found to affect the legs, feet and toes but could occur on the face, arms, hands and fingers as well. If left untreated the infection could spread to the lymph nodes and the blood stream, requiring hospitalisation.
What is cellulitis?
Cellulitis is a common skin infection caused mostly by streptococcus and staphylococcus bacteria. It can affect the tissues beneath the skin. Though it can affect any part of the body such as the face, arms, hands and fingers it usually affects the legs, feet and toes. Cellulitis can also affect just one side of the body. Anyone can contract cellulitis, but persons with skin wounds, or compromised immune systems, which allows the bacteria to enter easily, are at higher risk. Poor skin hygiene may also be a contributing factor. Cellulitis is not contagious but if untreated or if severe, it can spread to tissue under the skin, the lymph nodes and the bloodstream.
Symptoms and treatment
Infected skin may appear slightly discoloured, and warm to touch. As the infection spreads, the discolouration darkens and the skin swells and becomes tender. Apart from swelling and warmth, the infection could be painful. Affected persons could have fever, feel fatigued, experience chills, develop spots on the skin, blisters filled with fluid and dimpling of the skin.
Treatment usually consists of a course of oral antibiotics. Severe cases may need hospitalisation and IV antibiotics.
Preventing relapses
Good skin hygiene can help prevent a relapse. It is necessary to wash hands regularly with soap and warm water. Cleaning and trimming finger and toenails and thoroughly drying the skin after a shower, wearing clean clothes and keeping small wounds clean can prevent the infection.
Cellulitis in India
An observational study by Tripta S. Bhagat, Luv Kumar, et al published in the The International Journal of Lower Extremity Wounds in March 2023 found that cellulitis was commonly seen in men, in the working age group. The mean age of those affected in the study was around 36 years. The affected were in field jobs, and among them 50% of the time, the risk factor for the condition was trauma. Other factors included diabetes mellitus and smoking. The commonest complication was abscess. While over half the persons required only conservative management the rest needed surgical intervention, requiring hospitalisation for five or more days.
What research has found
A 2023 multi-centre clinical study on 247 individuals,The natural history of antibiotic-treated lower limb cellulitis: analysis of data extracted from a multicenter clinical trial, by three O. Martin Williams, Fergus Hamilton and Richard Brindle, has thrown more light on how the bacterial infection is resolved.
The study found that while swelling reduced by half within 10 days of administering antibiotics and the size of the affected area also shrank to half its original size and a blood marker of the inflammation reached near-normal levels in all the participants, more than half the participants reported discomfort in the affected leg and around 14% of the participants said the pain was severe, ranking it 5 or greater on a scale of 1 to 10.
Residual symptoms can persist in some cases even after the course of antibiotics has been completed.
Home treatments include warm compresses to reduce swelling, elevating the leg to improve blood flow, compression socks and walking to reduce discomfort. Rest and refraining from touching the affected areas can also help.
It is, however, important to consult a doctor to have cellulitis treated and essential to complete the entire course of treatment as prescribed, in order prevent progression and complications.

Bollywood actor's Indian festival ad withdrawn after row over outfit
- Published
An Indian jewellery brand has removed their new advertisement for the upcoming festival of Rakshabandhan, also known as Rakhi, after backlash over the outfit worn by the female lead.
The ad featured popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon celebrating the Hindu festival in which sisters tie a thread called Rakhi over their brothers' wrists.
Sanon, who is seen in a cropped top, skirt and a drape, addressed her critics on Tuesday night saying "culture and traditions are in a woman's heart, not in her neckline!"
The row started earlier on Tuesday after actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut called the ad "intentionally creepy" and asked why someone would tie a Rakhi dressed in a bikini.
In her comments posted on social media, Ranaut did not name Sanon, but appeared to be referring to the actor.
"It is a wonderful time to be a woman, our closets are full of variety of clothes... From all the options that are available to us today why would you tie your brother a Rakhi in your bikini/under garments? Where are all your styling options? The advert looks intentionally creepy," she wrote.
Her remarks quickly drew attention online, with some users echoing her criticism of Sanon's outfit. Others objected to a scene in the advertisement in which the actor also tries a rakhi on her pet dog.
But Sanon also received support, including from Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, who defended her, saying what a woman chose to wear was her own decision. Others accused Ranaut of moral policing.
Some also pointed out that though Ranaut has been more conservative in her clothing in recent years after becoming a politician, she herself often wore short dresses and Western outfits in her films and at social gatherings.
Sanon responded to the critics in an Instagram story, calling out the mindset that questioned women for their sartorial choices. Like Ranaut, she did not name anyone directly.
"The essence of festivals is not in the clothes you wear, it is in the emotions and meaning you hold for the traditions... When will we stop telling women what to wear?? Ethnic fashion has evolved over the years, but still a woman's respect for her culture is measured with just her clothes!! Culture & Traditions are in her heart, not in her neckline!"
Sanon also addressed the issue of tying Rakhi to her pet, saying though the festival traditionally celebrates the bond between a brother and sister, its spirit was about protecting loved ones - which, for her, included her sister and her pet.
Despite her spirited defence, jewellery company Giva announced on Wednesday it was pulling the ad.
"We have the highest regard and deep respect for Indian culture, traditions and festivals. As a brand, we have always believed in celebrating these joyous moments with the entire family and this time we wanted to extend the love and celebration to our pets," Giva said in a statement, external on Instagram.
"If our recent advertisement has inadvertently hurt the sentiments of some segments of society, that was not our intent at all. Out of respect, we have withdrawn the advertisement from all media," it added.
Giva is not the first Indian brand to withdraw an ad after criticism on social media. In 2020, popular jewellery brand Tanishq withdrew an advertisement featuring an interfaith couple after it faced right-wing backlash online.
Debates over what women should - and shouldn't - wear have also repeatedly sparked controversy in India.
Last year, a beauty pageant contestant was commended for standing up to a group of men who tried to bully her and other contestants over the skirts and western dresses they were wearing.
In 2021, there was outrage after a 19-year-old student, who turned up in shorts to take an exam, was forced to wrap a curtain around her legs after the teacher objected to her clothes.
In the same year, thousands of women - and some men - shared photos of themselves wearing ripped jeans after the chief minister of the northern state of Uttarakhand criticised a woman for wearing them.

CIA chief in Moscow for unannounced talks, US media reports
- Published
The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has travelled to Moscow for unannounced talks, the BBC's US news partner CBS has reported.
John Ratcliffe reportedly arrived in the Russian capital earlier on Tuesday. Neither Washington or Moscow have confirmed the nature of the visit or who he was due to meet.
In-person talks between high-level American and Russian officials are rare.
BBC News has contacted the CIA, the White House and Pentagon for comment.
Flight tracking data confirmed a large US military aircraft travelled to Russia from the US via Latvia on Tuesday.
Footage posted on social media showed the C-17 transport plane approaching Moscow's Vnukovo international airport.
It departed Riga airport at 05:50 GMT and appears to have landed at around 07:04 GMT, according to data from FlightRadar24.
Footage on social media also purported to show a diplomatic motorcade travelling through Moscow.
The trip is thought to be Ratcliffe's first trip to Russia as CIA director, although he has maintained contact with his intelligence counterparts in Moscow.
He played a role in negotiations for the release of Russian-American citizen Ksenia Karelina's, who was jailed in Russia for over a year after being accused of providing support to Ukraine.
The CIA was also involved in a 2024 prisoner swap deal with Russia that saw the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, as well as former US marine Paul Whelan and Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva.
The US has had strained relations with Russia since it launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Since then, Russia has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions.
Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit the country during President Donald Trump's second term.
Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled.

Mass arrests in global crackdown on West African cyber-crime networks
- Published
Fifty-eight people linked to organised West African cyber-crime groups have been arrested in an operation across 22 countries and six continents.
Dubbed "Operation Jackal IV", it was co-ordinated by the global policing agency Interpol, targeting those behind romance and investment scams. It also identified 263 suspects.
Interpol said it was a response to the escalating global threat posed by these criminal networks - such as the feared Nigerian Black Axe group - believed to be behind a "significant share" of cyber-enabled financial fraud.
The operation also allowed analysis of emerging trends such as how these groups use sextortion to target minors, with victims as young as 14.
- The ultra-violent cult that became a global mafia 
  - Published13 December 2021
Operation Jackal IV - which took place between November 2025 and June 2026 - investigated how the groups laundered money and how financial fraud cyber crimes, such as cryptocurrency and email compromise fraud, were conducted.
Scams often targeted "retirees in English-speaking countries", Interpol said.
"By following illicit financial flows across borders, we are attacking the very lifeblood of organised crime and making it increasingly difficult for criminal networks to profit from their activities," Tomonobu Kaya, director of Interpol's financial crime centre, said in a statement.
"Operation Jackal IV demonstrates the power of international co-operation."
During the operation, Interpol helped with cross-border co-ordination and intelligence sharing.
It also provided support and specialised training for money-laundering investigations with the participating countries.
Interpol said many aspects of Jackal IV remained under investigation but preliminary outcomes included arrests in Argentina, Italy, Romania and South Africa.
In South Africa, seven sites linked to a syndicate involved in romance and investment scams were raided.
The policing agency was on scene in Johannesburg to support local authorities during the raids.
South African police made 39 arrests, seized $2.67m (£1.96m) and blocked 257 bank accounts.
As well as cyber-enabled fraud, the West African networks also participated in other serious and violent crimes, Interpol said.
Operation Jackal IV is one of multiple "Jackal" police operations that have taken place since 2022.
In 2024, Jackal III led to the arrests of 300 people linked to Black Axe and other affiliated groups.
Black Axe is a shadowy criminal network with trafficking, prostitution and killing operations around the world.
Nigeria is its main recruitment ground and many of its members are university educated and inducted during their schooling.

'0% chance' - Atletico hit back at Barca over Alvarez transfer row
- Published
Atletico Madrid insist there is "0% chance" of selling Julian Alvarez to Barcelona after club president Joan Laporta said they remain interested in signing the forward.
Alvarez has been the subject of intense transfer speculation this summer, and after being booed by Atletico supporters on Sunday during their draw with Villarreal, the 26-year-old missed training on Wednesday.
Reports say Alvarez was unwell, and Atletico have now condemned Laporta's latest video, published on Wednesday, which said Barcelona's €100m (£85.7m) offer remained on the table.
"This is not about money, it's about dignity. The player is being victimised, but the only victim in the Julian case is us," Atletico said.
"They have harmed us economically and socially. There is 0% chance of selling him to Barca.
"There is a campaign of many lies and half-truths. The only one paying for this is Atletico."
In the video, Laporta said the club had great respect for Atletico but the bid they lodged earlier this summer was still on offer.
Sources at Barcelona say they will keep trying to sign Alvarez, who joined Atletico from Manchester City in 2024, until the transfer window ends.
The comments come after weeks of increasingly complicated negotiations and public disagreements between the two clubs.
It also comes as Arsenal continue to show interest in the striker, who is viewed as the Gunners' dream transfer target.
But sources close to the situation say Alvarez still wants to stay in Spain.
- Alvarez's Arsenal dilemma amid summer's most bitter transfer tussle 
  - Published2 days ago
For now, Arsenal are sitting back and watching this unfold, as they become more realistic about their chances of signing Alvarez before next week's transfer deadline.
Alvarez started on the bench on Sunday but was jeered while warming up and there were even louder boos when he came on in the 66th minute.
He headed straight down the tunnel at full-time, rather than joining the rest of the team who were applauding the fans, which drew more boos.
Atleti boss Diego Simeone suggested afterwards that it was a pre-agreed club decision for the forward to head straight to the dressing room.
Speaking before Barcelona's match against Athletic Club on Thursday, head coach Hansi Flick declined to discuss Alvarez directly, saying: "I only want to speak about the situation of the club."
With deadline day approaching on 1 September, the war of words continues and the Argentine World Cup winner's future remains one of the biggest talking points of the transfer window.
Alvarez transfer saga – how did we get here?
The first offer on the table came from Barcelona in May, with reports suggesting the club had opened talks to sign Alvarez.
But in what seems to be a recurrent pattern, Atletico were absolutely adamant that they would not sell Alvarez to Barcelona.
In May, they made a series of social media posts brutally mocking Barca's pursuit of their player to millions of followers, saying they were victims of a "smear campaign".
Alvarez went to the World Cup with Argentina with his future already a major talking point.
Then, in June, in came another big offer from Atleti's city rivals, Real Madrid.
Los Blancos made a €150m (£130m) offer for Alvarez after president Florentino Perez promised supporters that he would make a €150m bid for an unnamed "Galactico" if re-elected.
The offer was rejected by Atletico, with Real Madrid pointing to Alvarez's €500m (£430m) release clause and saying Atletico had "expressed its gratitude for the proposal".
Again, Atleti responded with humorous social media posts, denying any gratitude and remaining adamant that Alvarez would not be sold to Barcelona.
After Argentina's win over Austria in June, Alvarez told media that he had spoken to Atletico and he said that "the best thing for everyone is a transfer", adding: "I want to fulfil my dream".
Those comments effectively confirmed that, despite Atletico's insistence that he was not for sale, the player himself was open to leaving and Barcelona and Paris St-Germain were among the clubs reportedly interested.
Barcelona's interest in Alvarez was driven by their need for a long-term successor to Robert Lewandowski, who left the club this summer.
But Atletico maintained they did not want to sell Alvarez, with chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin saying the club would not sell him "even for 200m euros (£170.8m)".

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) said that the United States would achieve nothing with its new round of economic sanctions, local media reported.
“With the measures that the government’s economic sectors have foreseen, America will not achieve anything with economic pressure at this stage, just as it was unable to achieve anything in the war,” Mr. Pezeshkian said, according to ISNA news agency.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday (August 24, 2026) laid out plans for the “economic asphyxiation” of Iran, warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign.
Iran’s leaders, however, have dismissed the impact of the new measures, having already endured decades-long crippling sanctions since shortly after the 1979 revolution.
“Our principle is understanding and resolving issues through interaction and negotiation, but at the same time, we will stand firm against economic pressures, as we have done so far and will continue to do,” Mr. Pezeshkian added.
Negotiations between Iran and the United States have stalled as the two foes wrangle over control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
Traffic through the vital waterway — which normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas exports — remains largely paralysed, disrupting global energy markets.
Iran has exerted control over the Hormuz strait since the outbreak of the war on February 28, and has sought to impose fees on vessels transiting the strait.
The United States wants the strait to return to its pre-war system of free navigation, and U.S. President Donald Trump has claimed that Washington “has total control” over the waterway.
But on Wednesday (August 26, 2026), Iran’s Revolutionary Guards countered, saying that Hormuz “is under our control, and... No vessel is able to pass through this waterway without Iran’s permission”.
“If America does not accept our conditions, the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened under any circumstances.”

Microsoft is officially announcing a new Xbox feature that will allow Xbox owners to digitize their existing physical game collections. The disc-to-digital feature, which The Verge exclusively revealed last month, is part of work that Microsoft is doing for game preservation and in preparation for the next generation of Xbox consoles.
Xbox announces disc-to-digital feature that digitizes your physical games
Xbox Insiders will get access to this new feature on August 31st.
“Most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games support this new feature,” explains Jason Ronald, VP of next generation at Xbox. “Players can claim a digital entitlement by inserting a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.” This digital entitlement is tied to the specific disc, and it will move from account to account if you swap the physical game with a friend or log in to a different Xbox profile and try to play a disc-based game.
Microsoft will start testing this new Xbox disc-to-digital feature with Xbox Insider testers on August 31st, followed by a broader rollout to Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles in the coming months. Once you have a digital version of an Xbox disc game, if supported you’ll also be able to access the game on PC through Xbox Play Anywhere, or stream it to multiple devices with Xbox Cloud Gaming.
A leaked memo from earlier this month revealed that publishers would have control over the Xbox disc-to-digital, so not every game will be supported initially. “We’re starting with thousands of titles, and we’ll continue to add more over time,” says Ronald. “While not every title will be available at launch, this is an important step toward a future where players can have greater confidence that the games they buy remain with them for years to come.”
The Xbox disc-to-digital feature arrives just weeks after Sony announced it’s killing all physical PlayStation game discs. New PlayStation games released after January 2028 will be digital-only, but it’s not yet clear if Microsoft will announce a similar end of production for Xbox discs. Either way, Sony hasn’t announced a similar feature for converting an existing physical library into a digital one.
Microsoft is also bringing Xbox and Xbox 360 games to PC, in a move that could allow the next Xbox console to play every Xbox game ever made.

The inaugural season of the European T20 Premier League (ETPL) is set to kick off at Sportpark Duivesteijn in Voorburg, the Netherlands, on Wednesday.
The six-team tournament will be played over the next three weeks, with a total of 32 matches, including a qualifier and the final, scheduled for September 19 and 20, respectively.
What is the format?

Bitdefender VPN was reliable in my time using it, as well. I didn’t experience any connection drop-outs or periods of unusually slow performance.
These are solid results, though not the best. For example, I saw slightly better speeds (up to 540 Mbps, the same as when not connected to the VPN) while using IVPN with the WireGuard protocol enabled, for example.
Still, Bitdefender is plenty fast, very reliable, and I can’t say I found the gap in performance noticeable outside of in particular testing. I expect that most people will find the data rates provided by Bitdefender VPN to be more than adequate.
Privacy Promises and Compromises
Unlike Mullvad, a privacy-pilled alternative that positions itself as a tool against mass surveillance, Bitdefender VPN focuses more on avoiding geo-restrictions, ads, cookies, tracking, and Wi-Fi sniffing. There’s nothing wrong with that approach, but if you want a service that puts the P in VPN, you should look elsewhere.
Bitdefender’s VPN is provided through a partnership with IPVanish. IPVanish provides the infrastructure, while Bitdefender provides the client software, branding, customer service, and so on. It's worth mentioning, as IPVanish took a reputation hit back in 2018 when it handed user logs to the US Department of Homeland Security. This occurred in 2016 and happened despite having a no-logs policy.
However, IPVanish ownership has exchanged hands several times since then, and it’s now owned by media company Ziff Davis. IPVanish has undergone a number of successful independent, no-log audits, the most recent of which occurred in 2025. IPVanish also publishes a transparency report showing the volume of requests it has received from law enforcement and the data it has provided in response.
That’s good news, but wrinkles remain. IPVanish is a US company, and US law is pretty strict when it comes to law enforcement demands for data. IPVanish can’t provide what it doesn’t log, but privacy nerds often prefer VPN companies in less draconian jurisdictions.
It’s also unclear how Bitdefender’s service interact with IPVanish’s no-logs policy. Bitdefender obviously retains at least some information about the user, because a Bitdefender account is required to use the VPN, and users have to pay with a credit card. Bitdefender has some customer service information about its no-log policy, but the specific wording means this could be referring to the IPVanish audit.
Whether any of this matters depends on what privacy means to you. If you want an extra layer of network security to ward against trackers and prevent issues on compromised Wi-Fi connections, then Bitdefender VPN will do the job. However, Bitdefender VPN isn’t going to meet your needs if you’re worried about nation-state tracking or want to move across the web in near secrecy.
Conclusion
Bitdefender’s VPN is an easy-to-use service that works best for people with basic expectations for what a VPN should offer. It provides typical features and delivers solid network performance at a competitive price. It’s not the ultimate VPN for privacy and it’s lacking a few features some people will want, like Linux support and a static IP option.
Pricing might push you toward Bitdefender VPN—at least for the first year. The introductory offer of $35 for a year of service is an outstanding value. Just remember to check pricing again before it’s time to renew, as Bitdefender’s pricing after the first year is less enticing.

Govt plans standards exemptions to boost semiconductor investment in India
The proposed mechanism is expected to address regulatory concerns raised by foreign investors, particularly Japanese companies, and speed up the setting up of advanced manufacturing facilities in India.
The government is preparing major policy changes to make India more attractive for investment in semiconductors and other high-tech industries, with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal announcing plans for a framework to exempt select equipment and components from mandatory Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification.
The proposed mechanism is expected to address regulatory concerns raised by foreign investors, particularly Japanese companies, and speed up the setting up of advanced manufacturing facilities in India.
The government is working on a system under which specific industries, companies, projects or products could receive exemptions from BIS certification when required.
Such targeted relief could significantly reduce the time taken to procure specialised machinery, equipment and critical components from overseas.
The move is particularly important for semiconductor manufacturing, where plants depend on highly specialised machinery, gases, chemicals and electronic components, often produced by only a limited number of global suppliers.
Delays in obtaining certification for even a single critical component can disrupt the supply chain and affect project timelines.
A faster exemption process could therefore help companies source essential equipment more quickly and accelerate investments in India.
QUALITY CONTROL CONCERNS
Japanese companies have raised concerns over quality control orders and regulatory procedures while considering investments in India.
The proposed framework is expected to provide greater regulatory flexibility while helping ensure that critical high-tech projects are not held up because alternatives to specialised imported components may not be readily available.
The changes could also give fresh momentum to India's semiconductor ambitions.
The government has approved 13 projects under SEMICON-1, which are expected to lay the foundation for around USD 19 billion in investments. Another USD 15 billion has been committed under SEMICON-2, with the government hoping to catalyse overall investments of about USD 50 billion across the sector.
WHY JAPAN HOLDS KEY
Japan is seen as a key partner in this effort because of its strengths in semiconductor equipment, materials, specialty chemicals, industrial gases and precision manufacturing. India, meanwhile, brings a large market, engineering talent and strong chip-design capabilities.
The two countries are looking to combine these strengths to develop a broader semiconductor ecosystem and deepen cooperation across the supply chain.
PIYUSH GOYAL’S JAPAN VISIT
The policy push comes during Goyal's August 24-27 visit to Japan, where he is leading a delegation of more than 220 Indian industry representatives. He has met Japanese government and corporate leaders and sought to expand investment and industrial cooperation.
India is looking at doubling the presence of Japanese companies from the current level of around 1,500, with Goyal saying, "We want 1,580 companies like Suzuki to emerge from India."
His engagements included meetings with Sumitomo Corporation, Meiji Seika Pharma and Mitsubishi Corporation, while discussions with Japanese industry bodies focused on sectors ranging from capital goods and automobiles to strategic technologies.
Cooperation in semiconductors, critical minerals and pharmaceuticals also figured prominently during the visit.
The government has set a target of attracting 10 trillion yen in Japanese investment over the next decade.
Goyal has assured Japanese industry that central and state governments will extend full support to investors in semiconductors as well as emerging sectors such as AI, quantum computing and data centres.
Going forward, the proposed BIS exemption framework could become a key part of India's effort to remove bottlenecks for high-tech manufacturing.
If implemented effectively, it could help bring in more Japanese and other foreign investments while accelerating the development of a domestic ecosystem for semiconductor machinery, materials, components and advanced technologies.

Volvo is updating three of its electric vehicles with new hazard alerts to warn drivers when there are animals or vulnerable road users ahead. The new connected safety features are based on Volvo’s cars talking to one another, as opposed to crowdsourced alert systems used by popular navigation tools like Google Maps and Waze.
Volvo’s cars will warn one another about hazards in the road
The company’s connected safety alerts will now warn drivers when there are animals, pedestrians, cyclists, roadwork, or accidents ahead.
The alerts work by using connected vehicle data from Volvo’s fleet of passenger vehicles in Europe, the US, and Canada. The car’s sensors and cameras are tuned to identify certain risks on the road. When one Volvo spots a hazard, it automatically logs the location and sends it to Volvo’s servers. Alerts are then sent to all other Volvo vehicles traveling along that same road. The alerts still depend on the car being connected to the cloud and the road existing in the map database, but Volvo’s newer EVs have plenty of computing power to handle the real-time processing requests.
Volvo said it’s updating its EVs with alerts for four types of hazards: large animals; vulnerable road users, like pedestrians or cyclists; roadwork; and accidents. The new alerts are coming to the Volvo EX90, ES90, and EX60. Volvo says it has 1 million vehicles on the road today with connected safety alert capabilities. And it shares its alert data with traffic management centers, as well as other vehicle brands, so its not just Volvo branded vehicles that are benefiting.
Volvo has used connected vehicle technology to power some of its hazard warnings since 2016. The Swedish company’s cloud-based system, developed in partnership with Ericsson, warns drivers of slippery roads ahead based on feedback from steering, braking, and acceleration sensors. It also notifies nearby vehicles when another car has activated its hazard lights indicating that another driver may be in a dangerous or unexpected position on the road.
In addition, Volvo said that the EX90 would be getting Spatial Audio support for Apple CarPlay users. This will allow drivers to “enjoy a multi-dimensional and immersive sound experience that places music and vocals around the cabin,” the company says.

Over 72 roads blocked by boulder falls as Uttarakhand braces for heavy rain
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of thunderstorms, lightning and intense spells of rain at isolated places over the next few days in Uttarakhand.
More than 72 roads were blocked by landslides and boulder falls across Uttarakhand on Wednesday as several parts of the state received light to moderate rainfall, while the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of thunderstorms, lightning and intense spells of rain at isolated places over the next few days.
Pithoragarh, Nainital and Chamoli were the worst-affected districts, with 14, 12 and 10 road closures, respectively. The IMD’s Dehradun centre has issued a yellow alert, forecasting thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and intense to very intense spells of rainfall at isolated places in the state’s hilly districts from August 27 to September 1.
According to district-wise data, Pithoragarh reported the highest number of road closures at 14, followed by Nainital with 12 and Chamoli with 10. Pauri reported seven closures, while Bageshwar, Rudraprayag, Tehri and Uttarkashi recorded six each. Dehradun had four closed roads and Haridwar one, while Almora, Champawat and Udham Singh Nagar reported no closures. The disruptions, mainly in the hill districts, have affected connectivity across the state, taking the total number of closed roads and routes to 72.

Police are on the hunt for a seafood swindler after 400,000 oysters were allegedly stolen from a farm at a river on the New South Wales mid-north coast.
About 320 bags of juvenile oysters, worth an estimated $350,000, were taken from an oyster farm in Scotts Creek, Oxley Island, earlier this year, according to NSW police.
Officers received a report of the theft on Tuesday morning and are urging members of the public with CCTV or dashcam footage to come forward.
Latitude 31 Oyster Co, which runs a Sydney rock oyster farm on Manning River adjacent to Scotts Creek, on Tuesday revealed it had been the target of a “massive” oyster theft that had been reported to police.
“Oyster theft impacts far more than just the individual farmer. It affects our businesses, our families and the reputation of the entire NSW oyster industry,” the business wrote in a social media post.
“There are a lot of good people in this industry, and we know farmers look out for each other.”
The business urged the community to look out for anyone who is trying to move, or has suddenly come into possession of, a large quantity of cocktail or bistro-sized oysters.
Latitude 31 Oyster Co said the stolen oysters were not ready for immediate sale and would need to be grown for another four to six months.
Guardian Australia has contacted Latitude 31 Oyster Co to confirm the thefts are the same.
Oyster farmer Gary Rodley, who owns Tathra Oysters on the NSW south coast, said fully grown oysters could be worth significantly more, estimating they could fetch about $1.50 to $2 a piece.
The age of the stolen molluscs and the amount taken suggests the culprit could be a fellow producer, he said.
“That’s not a theft where someone’s getting a feed of oysters,” he said.
“That’s disturbing to think that it might be a one of our peers in the industry.
“It’s a very high-risk activity that person’s carrying out, and I would fancy that they would come unstuck very quickly doing that sort of thing.”
A Manning River oyster farmer, who wished to remain anonymous, said there had been a recent shortage of the coveted Sydney rock oyster.
Major flooding in 2021 and 2025 wiped oyster stocks in the region, and because Sydney rock oysters are farmed on a three-year cycle, it could take another two years before farmers’ incomes stabilise.
“The worst case scenario is it could be someone within the industry that has had a shortfall, who has gone past that area of the river and knows it only gets used certain times of year, and they’ve gone ‘they’ll never know until they get back’,” he said.
Theft is not uncommon in the Manning River area, but when he has been targeted, his oysters were taken by locals who had all year to scope out the area.
The farmer took the issue into his own hands and bought an artificial oyster with a tracker from France that cost more than $2,000.
It allowed him to take a thief to court in 2022, where the culprit was fined $500.
Many oyster farmers, including Rodley, have bought surveillance equipment to act as a deterrent as demand for Sydney rock oysters has grown.
“They’re a rare oyster that only grow up and down the New South Wales coastline, so they’re a very, very small percentage of the world’s oyster crop,” he said.
“It’s regarded as probably the best flavoured oyster in the world by a lot of people – they’re a very flavoursome oyster and highly regarded as a table oyster that’s eaten natural.
“That’s a particular set of circumstances that a lot of people value highly.”
A crime scene has been established and police investigations are ongoing.

Stokes recorded television news for more than three decades, amassing a collection of more than 70,000 tapes.
The duration of her recordings has not been definitively established.
In 2026, posts on social media sites highlighted an important historical figure: activist Marion Stokes. The posts claimed Stokes recorded around 300,000 hours of television — purportedly one of the largest known personal archives of such material.
The claim circulated on TikTok, Reddit and Threads. A TikTok video claimed to detail her remarkable life:
Marion Stokes started recording television in 1979 because she noticed something that bothered her deeply. TV networks were erasing their own archives — wiping old footage to save money and storage space. Nobody was keeping the record. So she decided she would. For 35 years, she ran up to eight VCRs simultaneously in her Philadelphia home, recording around the clock. News, commercials, sitcoms, local broadcasts, breaking events. The tapes ran out every six to eight hours. She almost never missed a change. Friends and family described rushing home from dinner so she could swap them out. By the time she died on December 14, 2012 — as Sandy Hook coverage filled every channel — she had accumulated 71,000 VHS and Betamax tapes. Over 300,000 hours of television. She bought nine additional apartments just to store them all. Historians now call it one of the most valuable media archives ever created. An unfiltered record of how news was told, how narratives shifted, and what powerful institutions chose to quietly walk back or change over time.
It's true that Stokes recorded news footage onto tens of thousands of tapes, but the duration of that footage has not been definitively established. Therefore we've rated this claim a mixture of true and undetermined information.
Stokes was a Black social justice activist and a television producer. According to a profile of Stokes in Atlas Obscura, in 1975, she purchased a Betamax magnetic videotape recorder through which she began her archival project. By 1980 she began recording full time on multiple VCRs, starting with two or three and moving on to eight.
While many sources say she started recording in 1975, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported that she began intermittently taping television programming in 1976. But according to her son, Michael Metelits, who spoke to the Inquirer in a number of interviews, her taping became constant at the onset of the Iran hostage crisis in 1979. She was also bolstered by the founding of CNN in 1980 that ushered in an era of 24-hour news coverage.
Her recordings continued until her death in 2012, and covered nine news stations, according to the 2019 documentary "Recorder: The Marion Stokes Project."
According to the documentary website, her recordings truly began in 1979. Regardless of her start date, she was recording for more than 30 years, in a manner that her son described as part of her impulse to save and hoard, but also "a form of activism."
The documentary, which was shown at the Tribeca Film Festival and received critical acclaim, described the importance of her archiving:
Before "fake news" Marion was fighting to protect the truth by archiving everything that was said and shown on television. The public didn't know it, but the networks were disposing their archives for decades into the trashcan of history. Remarkably Marion saved it, and now the Internet Archive will digitize her tapes and we'll be able to search them online for free.
This is a mystery in the form of a time capsule. It's about a radical Communist activist, who became a fabulously wealthy recluse archivist. Her work was crazy but it was also genius, and she would pay a profound price for dedicating her life to this visionary and maddening project.
According to early reports in 2013, Stokes had around 140,000 VHS tapes that contained news coverage of revolutions, political scandals and more. Her son donated the tapes to the Internet Archive — a nonprofit group known for its vast online archive — which planned to digitize everything and make it available to the public. The Internet Archive lowered this estimated number of tapes to 40,000 as it began receiving containers of them from Stokes' family.
A correction to a Fast Company report on the digitization process was published in Poynter in 2014: "And there aren't 140,000 VHS tapes, as Fast Company and Poynter wrote back in November. Just 40,000. The family overestimated."
The Internet Archive also reached out to Fast Company with an update:
The Internet Archive received four shipping containers of Stokes' tapes in December. After conducting a sample inventory, it realized that the family's initial estimate of the number of tapes was incorrect. The collection is about 40,000 tapes large. "I think it's daunting when confronted with many storage containers, 20- or 30-feet deep, to figure it out," Macdonald says about why the mistake was made.
However, in 2021, the Internet Archive tweeted about a larger number of tapes with a photograph of when they were delivered, saying there were more than 70,000:
Today, the tapes can be found in the Internet Archive's vast collection, along with documents related to Stokes' life.
We heard from Roger MacDonald, founder of the Internet Archive's TV News Archive, who gave us more up-to-date information on Stokes' collection:
Our current best count of video cassettes in the Marion Stokes TV Archive is 71,716. Although each has notations on the spine indicating programs recorded and dates, we have not counted the number of programs, nor their durations.
[…]
We are looking forward to the time when we have sufficient funds to really making a dent in digitizing the vast collection and making it available online in our library.
So while it is true Stokes had more than 70,000 tapes in her collection, the duration of those tapes has not been determined.
Stokes' collection is certainly not the largest such archive in the world. That distinction may belong to Vanderbilt University, which claims to have "the world's most extensive and complete archive of television news." The university has "been recording, preserving and providing access to television news broadcasts of the national networks since August 5, 1968."
UCLA claims to have "the largest university-held collection of motion pictures and broadcast programming." Dartmouth's Media Ecology Project ranks UCLA's Film and Television Archive as "the second largest moving image archive in the United States after the Library of Congress, and the world's largest university-based media archive."
Atlas Obscura describes Stokes' archive as "the only comprehensive collection preserving this period [the mid-1970s to 2012] in television media history," and some reports say this is the largest known archive of television made by an individual. This assessment is possibly correct, given that recording all that material from one's own home was particularly unheard of at that time. We are unaware of another personal project with this extent of archival footage.

Insurance covered the rebuild of her house after a fire. Why didn’t the bank release the money on time?
Lawyer seeing an increase in insurance payouts not aligning, leaving homeowners to cover shortfalls
The fire that destroyed Antonina Gladkova's property at the beginning of 2024 was just the beginning of years of frustration and financial stress that's cost her tens of thousands of dollars and left her wanting to warn other homeowners about what's in their mortgage agreements when it comes to insurance claims.
But the fire "was just the first nightmare," she said. "It became worse."
At first, Gladkova says she was relieved with the smooth process of dealing with her insurance company, which covered the full cost to rebuild her half of the semi-detached house in Georgetown, Ont.
But, her mortgage provider didn't dole out the insurance payments on pace with her contractor's invoices, and now she says she and her boyfriend are out tens of thousands of dollars and on the hook for a private mortgage they had to get to cover the shortfalls and keep construction going amid costly delays.
"We were absolutely outraged," she said.
While it's routine for insurance payments to be released in installments through a homeowner's mortgage lender, legal experts say situations like Gladkova's are becoming more common. That's why she's warning others about her experience in hopes of preventing it from happening again.
"The whole system doesn't work. And that's why I want people to know … be prepared," she said.
'A chicken and egg situation'
In February 2024, a fire broke out in the neighbouring half of Gladkova's semi-detached property. Her neighbour tragically died in the fire, which spread to her half, completely destroying it. Gladkova, who originally lived in the home, had been renting it out for several years after she moved in with her boyfriend.
Just over a year after the fire, the insurance payment to rebuild the home was approved at just over $508,000. Because they had a mortgage, the lender, Simplii Financial, was responsible for releasing the funds.
The couple's contractor required the first payment of $101,600, but Simplii only released $25,000, according to bank statements reviewed by CBC News.
After the couple brought up the issue, Simplii, which is part of CIBC, released another $25,000 as part of what they called a "one-time exception." But the couple was still 50 per cent short.
Gladkova says the inital process was for the bank to release funds based on invoices from the builder and confirmation of completed work. But that would require the contractor, who she says was chosen by the insurance company, to finance the work upfront.
"You cannot build without the money. So it's like a chicken and egg situation," Gladkova said.
The couple filed a formal complaint with Simplii, requesting that the bank release an additional $51,600 so they could pay the invoice in full and keep construction going. The bank declined.
Gladkova says they didn't have enough money to pay the difference, so they got a private mortgage with a 10 per cent interest rate.
After the formal complaint, documents show Simplii changed its process to provide funds based on progress reports of the work that was completed. For example, if 20 per cent of the work was completed, Simplii would have provided 20 per cent of the total insurance payment.
But, emails between Gladkova and Simplii show the bank began making the calculation on the first insurance cheque rather than the total insurance payout, which Gladkova says resulted in the couple consistently being about 35 per cent short on paying the contractor.
Simplii did eventually release all of the money, including through another additional exception payment this past April to cover a shortfall for the third construction invoice.
The rebuild was completed this past June, about six months behind schedule, according to the construction contract.
Gladkova says the couple has paid around $15,000 in interest on the private mortgage and counting, plus thousands to set up the private mortgage and legal costs.
There's still an outstanding balance of about $19,000 owed to the contractor as a result of delays because the couple didn't have funds to pay him on time, Gladkova says.
She says that because of the private mortgage and the insurance payouts not keeping pace, the amount they owed "accumulated and skyrocketed in no time."
Simplii's response
In a statement, Simplii spokesperson Kira Smylie says the company empathizes with clients managing property damage and that "wherever possible, we work with our clients to provide flexibility, and we did so in this case."
Smylie also said Simplii's mortgage terms allow the bank to determine how insurance proceeds are applied.

"Before finalizing the payment terms with a contractor, clients should confirm the payment schedule with us so they can make informed decisions," she said.
Gladkova says she wants to warn others about how vague some mortgage agreements are written. She says that had the bank told them they would be responsible for any shortfalls, the couple would have made other arrangements.
How to protect yourself
Standard mortgage provisions require insurance money be paid to the lender, which will then release the money on a schedule, because the lender has an interest in the property and wants to ensure the funds are used to rebuild it, according to real estate and home insurance lawyers.
Fy Virani, the founder of Virani Law, which specializes in home insurance claims, says situations like Gladkova's that result in payment schedules not alligning are occurring more often. He says that's because lenders are exerting tighter control over insurance payouts since there are now more total loss claims from fires and floods.
"We're running into more and more total losses as a result of fires and floods," he said. "So the result becomes this communication gap between these entities that aren't used to being on the same page."
Virani says in order to prevent this, property owners should establish clear and open communication with lenders, contractors and insurance companies to ensure all parties are on the same page and that payment schedules align before construction begins.
"It's very hard to fix once money is already moving," he said.
Filing complaints
At the end of 2025, Gladkova filed a complaint with the Ombudsman for Banking Services and Investments (OBSI), which is an independent and impartial Canadian organization that helps resolve disputes between banks, investment firms and customers.
Gladkova wanted Simplii to compensate them for the interest on the private mortgage and $4,000 in fees that came along with it.

She says the OBSI completed its investigation last June and found that while Simplii is not responsible for the extra costs incurred, and was not bound by the agreement the couple reached with the contractor, the bank did cause extraordinary distress and inconvenience by not explaining to the couple that they may need additional financing to complete the project.
The OBSI recommended that Simplii give the couple $500 in compensation, which the couple did not accept.
"It was a slap in the face," Gladkova said.
In a statement, the OBSI said its complaint resolution process is confidential and cannot comment on an individual complaint.
Gladkova has since filed a complaint with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, which supervises federal external complaint bodies, including banks and the OBSI. She hopes to see changes to mortgage agreements so banks will release insurance payments directly to contractors.
"Hopefully, this can be fixed," she said. "No one should experience this as it was life changing."

Life can often become a long list of obligations. Work, money, security, all things someone needs to build a life, often take time to acquire, taking away from life itself. An actual life, filled with people, joys and the moments that make it matter, is something that many lose sight of in this pursuit.
“Don't get so busy making a living that you forget to make a life”- Dolly Parton
The quote above comes from Dolly Parton (1946-2026). It is widely cited and appears in collections of her sayings. The line specifically reflects a philosophy of gratitude, something that ran through her work and public life.
The American country music legend, songwriter, actor, and philanthropist was considered one of the world's most beloved entertainers. She passed away on 25 August, leaving behind a legacy built on her warmth, wit and legendary body of work.
Here, Parton distinguishes between two easily confused concepts: earning a living and earning a life. She says, making a living is the practical business of survival, while making a life is everything that living was meant to be for: relationships, joy, meaning and rest, everything that money exists to support rather than replace.
The word “busy” is the warning here. The danger is not ambition or hard work, but letting themselves consume so much attention that the life they're supposed to be serving quietly disappears. People often say they'll start living life at a certain point in their careers or once they've earned a certain amount of money, only to find that the earnings never end.
The contemporary world rewards productivity and income, with worth often being compared against such. Parton's line serves as a gentle correction, not dismissing the need to earn, but insisting that earning is a means to an end, but not the end itself. The busyness that feels like success left unchecked can crowd out the very things that make success so desirable.
This isn't, however, an argument against hard work itself, as Parton herself was famously hard-working. The point here is about balance, making sure that the pursuit of living doesn't permanently postpone the life it is meant to fund.
A living exists to support a life, not to replace it.
2. Beware the word "later"
The plan to start living once you have earned enough tends to postpone living forever.
3. Busyness is not the same as a full life
Being constantly occupied can quietly crowd out everything that gives life meaning.
4. Protect time for people and joy
Relationships and rest are not rewards for finishing your work; they are the work of a life.
5. Balance is a choice, not an accident
Space for a life rarely appears on its own; it has to be kept deliberately.

Shakira and Burna Boy’s “Dai Dai” was written and recorded to coincide with the World Cup, and the tune has far outlasted the soccer tournament. The collaboration remains one of the biggest hits in the United Kingdom, where it appears on four rosters and lives within the top two on every one of them.
“Dai Dai” is once again blocked from the summit on nearly every ranking where it appears, with both Shakira and Burna settling for second place across the board.
Shakira and Burna Boy Sit at No. 2 on Four Charts
“Dai Dai” currently sits at No. 2 on all four U.K. charts where it appears, though it takes a different route to that position on each roster. The collaboration holds steady in second place on the Official Singles chart, the most important songs ranking in the nation. It slips one rung to No. 2 on the Official Streaming tally while returning to that same high point on both the Official Singles Sales and Official Singles Downloads charts.
“Dai Dai” Is Blocked by a Historic No. 1
On the Official Singles chart, which ranks the most-consumed songs of any style in the U.K. using both streaming activity and sales, “Dai Dai” is comfortable once again at No. 2. The collaboration remains stuck behind “Rein Me In,” the historic team-up between Sam Fender and Olivia Dean.
That tune was originally a solo cut by Fender, but after Grammy winner Dean hopped on board a remix, it rose to No. 1. “Rein Me In” has since shattered the all-time record for the most weeks spent atop the Official Singles ranking and recently became the first composition to manage 20 frames in charge.
Shakira and Burna Boy’s Smash Returns to Its Sales Peak
“Dai Dai” returns to No. 2 on both the Official Singles Downloads and Official Singles Sales charts after sitting at Nos. 3 and 4, respectively, last week. The collaboration has already reached second place on both purchase-focused rosters, but has never climbed any higher.
This frame, Shakira and Burna come in behind “Move Into the Sun,” an electronic dance cut fronted by producer Hugh and featuring Imael Angel and Ultra Naté. Last week’s winner, Madonna and Kylie Minogue’s “Love Sensation,” steps back only a few rungs after dominating just days ago.
Shakira and Burna Boy Have Both Hit No. 1 in the U.K. Before
Both Shakira and Burna have conquered the Official Singles chart in the past. Burna led the charge for three frames back in 2019 alongside Ed Sheeran and Stormzy with “Own It.” Shakira has ruled with a pair of collaborations, first hitting No. 1 with Wyclef Jean on “Hips Don’t Lie” and then returning to the summit a year later with Beyoncé on “Beautiful Liar,” which spent nearly a month running the show.
“Dai Dai” is now tied with Shakira’s first U.K. hit, “Whenever, Wherever,” which also peaked at No. 2 more than 20 years ago.
Burna Boy Is Still Chasing Two Firsts
Both Shakira and Burna are looking for their first champion on the Official Singles Sales chart. “Dai Dai” marks Shakira’s first top 10 on that ranking, while Burna previously reached the region with “Own It,” which stalled at No. 3.
Burna is also hoping to earn his first leader on the Official Singles Downloads tally, where “Dai Dai” already represents his career best showing. Shakira has ruled that list before with both “Hips Don’t Lie” and “Beautiful Liar,” as apparently something about lying works perfectly for Shakira, and audiences never fail to eat it up.
Shakira and Burna Boy Already Reached No. 1 on the Streaming List
“Dai Dai” has already scored both Shakira and Burna their first No. 1 on the Official Streaming chart. The smash marks Shakira’s first top 10 on the streaming-focused roster, while Burna has racked up four appearances within the highest tier. He previously missed out on ruling by one rung with “Own It,” while his own “Last Last” and “Location,” a collaboration with rapper Dave, also found their way into the competitive region.

PGA Tour play-off shake-up a 'big swing' - McIlroy
- Published
Back-to-back Masters champion Rory McIlroy believes the PGA Tour are giving fans what they want by introducing matchplay to their end-of-season play-offs.
PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp confirmed on Thursday that from 2028 the Tour Championship will be played across two weeks, at two different courses, and adopt a head-to-head format.
World number two McIlroy, who is a three-time winner of the FedEx Cup, feels the return of matchplay to the PGA Tour for the first time since 2023 shows fans have been listened to by the decision-makers.
"I think the PGA Tour and the Future Competition Committee and Brian and everyone involved have really taken on board what the fans have been calling for and have wanted, which is matchplay," said the Northern Irishman, 37.
"Brian took me through the plan last week for the first time. I didn't really know anything about it. It's certainly different.
"Two weeks, two different venues, but it's cool. I think they've taken a big swing, and conceptually, I think I really like it."
The FedEx Cup play-offs have have gone through numerous iterations across their two decades, presently consisting of a three-event strokeplay series which begins with the top 70 players from the season-long points list.
This week's concluding Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta will have a $40m (£29.3m) purse, and while the events have undoubtedly been lucrative for players, there have been consistent questions regarding fan engagement.
McIlroy added: "I think they've been great for players. Obviously we play for a ton of money, and it's sort of like the culmination of the entire season.
"The players have been rewarded. I think what the Tour are really trying to do is listen to the fans and what they want, and I think this idea of matchplay over two weeks is something that came mostly from what the people that watch golf wanted, so I think that's a really good thing."

Protests against caste-based reservations were held in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on 21 August and in Connaught Place on 23 August, 2026, under the banner of the online campaign ‘Reservation Hatao Andolan’ (here, here, here). Against this background, a video showing a massive crowd gathered is being widely shared on social media (here, here), claiming that it shows a huge turnout at an anti-reservation protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Let’s verify the claim made in the post.
Claim: The video shows a massive crowd gathered at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, in support of an anti-reservation protest.
Fact: The viral video shows devotees gathered during the Jagannath Rath Yatra in Puri, Odisha, on 16 July 2026, and is unrelated to the anti-reservation protest in Delhi. The claim made in the post is FALSE.
On performing a reverse image search using the key frames of the viral video led to an Instagram post uploaded on 18 July 2026 that carried the same video and identified it as visuals from the Rath Yatra in Puri. A comparison of the two videos showed identical visuals, including the massive crowd, the open space in the middle, and security personnel wearing blue uniforms.
The Puri Rath Yatra was held on 16 July 2026, while the anti-reservation protest at Jantar Mantar took place on 21 August 2026. Therefore, the viral video was available online well before the Delhi protest and cannot be footage from the protest.
Further, we found a video posted by ANI on 15 July 2026, a day before the Rath Yatra. The video showed security arrangements outside the Shree Jagannatha Temple in Puri ahead of the festival. The same open space and security personnel seen in the ANI video also appear in the viral video. A comparison between both visuals can be seen below.
To sum up, an old Puri Rath Yatra video is being shared as an anti-reservation protest at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

Quick Summary
Apple Maps uses simple icons for search, directions, map modes, current location, weather, saved places, offline maps, sharing ETA, reporting incidents, and more. This guide explains every symbol and button across the app’s main screens.
Apple Maps has steadily improved over the years, but it still needs to catch up with Google Maps, especially in places like global coverage, public transport options, offline navigation, real-time traffic data, and much more. But if you are using an iPhone, unless you use Google Maps even on iOS, like me, Apple Maps is the default and the best choice for most people.
Apple Maps is cleaner and more properly integrated with the other Apple ecosystems. If you live in a place where Apple Maps goes one-on-one with Google Maps, then you shouldn’t even look further than Apple Maps for your navigation.
However, if you are a beginner or switching to Apple Maps from Google Maps, some icons and features can be confusing at first. Thanks to Apple, which kept the interface simpler, you don’t need an enormous learning curve to know how to use it. Most of the features are easy, and the icons are easily recognizable, but this guide helps you go even further by guiding you to know what every icon and feature means in Apple Maps.
This is a very comprehensive guide. It includes every Apple Maps screen and the meaning of every icon on each screen. You can also bookmark this page. In the future, if you get stuck on any icon you are wondering about, you can simply open this page and get to know what that icon means.
Table of Contents
What Do All the Icons and Symbols in Apple Maps Mean?
Apple Maps Home Screen Icon Meanings
- Map Options: Using this, you can change the Apple Maps options. Currently, Apple Maps supports Driving, Public Transport, Satellite, Explore, and much more. Also, depending on your selection, the map icon changes.
- Recenter Map: When you are navigating, you can recenter your position.
- Profile Menu: Tapping on your profile picture reveals the places you saved, reports, offline maps, your preferences, and much more.
- Voice Search: You can use the voice mode to search for places. This is just a voice mode and not a voice assistant.
- Search Maps: This is the main search bar for the maps where you can search for places, destinations, and much more.
- Compass: Apple Maps also comes with a native compass option that lets you easily find which direction you are pointing to. It only appears when you rotate the map and tap on it, pointing to the north direction.
- Weather & Air Quality: It shows the current temperature and local AQI for any location you are pointing to.
- Current Location: This shows your current location, and it blinks slightly, and the shadow cone is the direction you are pointing to.
Apple Maps Profile Screen
- Profile Menu: This is the same profile icon you see before swiping up for more details.
- Saved Places: Here you can view Home, Work, and saved places.
- Your Guides: Similarly, in this section you can see and open favorites and saved guides.
- Share My Location: A quick button lets you perform various tasks; the Share your current location button allows you to instantly share your current location.
- Mark My Location: This button instantly saves your current location.
- Report an Issue: This helps you report a Maps issue; you can report incidents, route issues, street issues, and much more.
Apple Maps Search Screen
- Search Maps: The main search bar allows you to search for different places with suggestions below.
- Voice Search: Use your voice; this is a speech-to-text converter, not a voice assistant.
- Close Search: You can close the search.
- Find Nearby: These are the default recommendations that all Apple Maps users see.
Apple Maps Place Details Screen
- Share Place: If you are looking at any particular location, you can tap on the share to share it with your friends or family.
- Close Details: Close the details card about this place.
- Download Map: You can save the map offline, but use it if you want to use your maps offline, especially when there is no internet in the place you are visiting.
- Directions: You can get directions to this place; it already shows you the current driving mode and the time to get there.
- Place Information: You can use the key details about the place, including its popular name, elevation, area, and much more.
- Add to Library: You can save this place.
- Add to Favorites: You can mark this place as a favorite.
- More Options: Open more place actions.
